rationale: I read the complete held EO 10656 (21 FR 859, Feb. 8, 1956, signed Feb. 6, 1956): secs. 1-5 establish the President's Board of Consultants on Foreign Intelligence Activities (appointment of outside members, review of foreign intelligence activities with semi-annual reports to the President, consultation with the Director of Central Intelligence, security undertakings and payment of allowances from the 'Special Projects' appropriation); it has no own term and no savings clause. I read the held full text of EO 10938 (26 FR 3951, May 6, 1961, signed May 4, 1961, Establishing the President's Foreign Intelligence Advisory Board): secs. 1-3 create the successor Board and sec. 4 states 'Executive Order No. 10656 of February 6, 1956, is hereby revoked.' That names EO 10656 by number and date and reaches all of it with no exception. The successor Board is a replacement, but the ending text is an express revocation, so this is not a successor-body inference. D6 self-check: a text search of the held full-run texts finds EO 10656 named only in EO 10938 (and its neighbouring-page extract in EO 10939, which carries the same page). EO 10938 was itself revoked by EO 11460 sec. 6 (held), which creates a new Board and does not mention EO 10656, so the revocation of the revoking order does not revive 10656. Nothing amends, extends or re-delegates EO 10656 between 1956 and 1961, and no own term ran out earlier. The OFR note 'Revoked by: EO 10938' agrees; the 1989 snapshot row is empty. Provisional NO hypothesis; the effective end (signing May 4, 1961, no later date stated) is not otherwise adjudicated.
